newsitem.title: FINLAND: CAUTIOUS FINNISH SMES WANT STABILITY - TT'S KOROMA.
newsitem.headline: CAUTIOUS FINNISH SMES WANT STABILITY - TT'S KOROMA.

text.p: Small- and medium-sized firms (SMEs) are still cautious and postpone investments although financial positions and confidence in the future have improved, the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT) said.
It said in a statement on Thursday that SMEs regard accelerating economic growth the main consideration in investments.
"Apart from that, the continuation of the recent moderate income policy was seen very important," TT director-general Johannes Koroma said.

"Particularly important was that corporate taxation will not in any way be tightened, including energy and environment taxes, and that the government would clearly announce that it scarps its planned depreciation reform," he addded.
But although the SMEs were still wary, the environment for increased invesments had clearly improved in many ways.
"Financial positions have improved, confidence in the economy has strengthened and the need for new capacity has also increased in some places," he said.

However, TT noted that the expected faster increase in the economy's output had not yet materialised. "Some publicly quoted companies' profit warnings have given a healthy reminder of that," Koroma said.
"The fact that SMEs postpone investment decisions clearly signals the general uncertainty that companies still have after the recession," he said.
